findings.description: The user_data script embeds a literal AWS access key ID (AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMAAA) and secret access key in cleartext. User data is retrievable via instance metadata (IMDS) by anyone who can reach the instance, is stored in Terraform state, and is visible in the console/API, so these long-lived credentials are effectively disclosed and reusable until rotated. This host is also internet-facing (public subnet, port 22 open to the world), compounding the exposure.

Port 22 is open to 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administration of the portal instance to the entire internet. Combined with the same host carrying hard-coded AWS credentials, this provides attackers a direct brute-force/exploit path to a machine holding live credentials. SSH should be restricted to a trusted CIDR or reached via a bastion/SSM.

Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 on an instance launched in a public subnet, exposing the web service to the entire internet over cleartext HTTP. Traffic is unencrypted and unauthenticated, and there is no HTTPS listener or TLS termination defined anywhere in this configuration.

The EBS volume has no encrypted = true setting, so data on the attached portal disk is stored unencrypted (snapshots taken from it are likewise unencrypted). Encryption at rest should be enabled for any volume holding portal data.

The netflow archive bucket has no server-side encryption configuration (no aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration and no default encryption), leaving VPC flow log data stored unencrypted at rest.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block and no account-level restriction is defined, and force_destroy = true permits deletion of contents. Without Block Public Access and ACL/bucket-policy hardening, the flow log archive (which reveals network topology and traffic metadata) can be made publicly readable.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance launched in this subnet (including aws_instance.portal_server) to receive a public IP by default, making it directly reachable from the internet and bypassing any intent to keep instances private.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true makes this subnet public, so any instance/service placed in it is automatically assigned a routable public address and exposed to the internet.
This snapshot is taken from aws_ebs_volume.portal_server_disk, which is unencrypted; no independent encryption is configured, so the backup is stored as cleartext data at rest.
